key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving electronic uniformity, showing that morphological irregularity need not imply optoelectronic disorder.
engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a route to more durable perovskite photovoltaics without requiring smoother film surfaces.
method: Form Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium cations.
Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare pristine and capped films before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films showed enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more spatially uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, with homogeneity largely preserved during accelerated aging.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify device-efficiency gains or establish whether accelerated-aging results translate to long-term operating stability.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
